Issue Number: close #45793

Problem Summary:
When the upstream set the column count limit to any value larger than the default one, the downstream would be not able to restore the data for DDL check error.
### What is changed and how it works?
use the max value as the default value for br.

issue_context.title: failed to restore DDL when upstream has some different limit config from default value
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
1. upstream, set some limit config, suche as table-column-count, to its max value.
2. create a table with too many column or index.
3. backup
4. restore to downstream
<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
1. success
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
failed to restore for DDL check error.
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)
master
<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

review_comments: seems fail on same type of mistake again. Do you consider to skip checks when creating table? like https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/522a00840385dfa43509a3af2bc79e6ff50252a8/ddl/schematracker/dm_tracker.go#L178

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/522a00840385dfa43509a3af2bc79e6ff50252a8/ddl/schematracker/dm_tracker_test.go#L50

DM has met a similar problem before, which is upstream MySQL has more capability than TiDB, so we use a special DDL implementation to apply DDL SQL.

There is a check before create table with DDL.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/57d778f0b1b6daebe0f330af2baa54e9e5310ea4/ddl/ddl_api.go#L2337-L2352

When use br, every check config is default value. If upstream has large value, for example set `TableColumnCountLimit` to 4000, the restore might be failed when there is a table with 4000 columns.
BR import the DDL package, but doesn't expose these configs.
